speaker: Ms Valerie Lee
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (a) whether there are updates in the Government’s clean energy solutions from the Pulau Ubin Micro-Grid test bed; (b) whether the Government is considering additional measures to lower electricity tariff charges for Pulau Ubin residents and business owners who are mostly the elderly; and (c) whether offering the regulated SP Electricity Tariff will be an option for Pulau Ubin residents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Residents may approach the relevant agencies to understand their eligibility for financial assistance.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: What has been the frequency of outages for the micro-grid?

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: When I am on the island chatting with them, they do share that they will request for compensation as outages damage their equipment, so I am concerned about inconveniences and the unseen costs that they might incur.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: I understand that there is no change in stance in trying to reduce electricity tariff there, so I understand 80 cents per kilowatt hours is fixed all the way to 2034, as reported in The Straits Times last year, which is a long time.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: What is the mechanism for these tariff changes?

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: The SP electricity tariff, as we know, is done every quarter.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: I am concerned that they might not have an equitable tariff adjustment mechanism.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: The third is, is there an exit clause in this arrangement without termination penalties?

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: I am concerned they might be penalised should they want to get out of this arrangement.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: And the last question, probably a bit more technical, but could the Ministry of Trade and Industry, and EMA consider using the framework of how the uniform Singapore electricity price is calculated based on a weighted average of all offtake modal prices, that considers many variables for residents and business owners on Ubin?

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Because as rightly pointed out, it is almost negligible in the whole system demand of things.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: I am concerned that they might be the only residents in the whole country who do not have a fair price to essential services like electricity.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: First of all, I would like to emphasise that the Pulau Ubin micro-grid users are already paying a lower electricity rate compared to the actual operating cost of this micro-grid.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: I think we also have to take a step back at this point to look at pricing of services and goods on Pulau Ubin.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: There is a very different treatment from mainland users who are using the SP grid.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: So, I think it is a bit difficult for us to just simply look at one piece of the cost of living issues and use that to determine then what we should do in terms of equalising the electricity tariff for the residents and the business consumers on Pulau Ubin.

speaker: Mr Speaker
